title: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal: On the Complexity of Evaluating Boolean Query DAGs
gist: Apple researchers prove that evaluating complex Boolean query DAGs over an inverted index is strictly P-Complete, show both standard evaluation strategies (Document-at-a-Time and Term-at-a-Time) hit hard theoretical walls (exponential blowup or full-universe scan cost), and introduce ComputePN, an algorithm that bounds evaluation time to O(|Q| · |U_active|) by decoupling negation from universe-scale materialization.

themes.theme: Search infrastructure as a bottleneck for AI agent reasoning

insights.claim: Modern AI agents increasingly compile complex, neuro-symbolic reasoning workflows into deeply nested, non-monotonic Boolean queries over text fields, pushing search/retrieval infrastructure to execute logic it was not originally designed for.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: As agentic AI systems proliferate, the query complexity they generate against retrieval backends is rising sharply, meaning search infrastructure providers (and any company embedding agents over its own search stack) face a looming performance/scalability problem that generic indices weren't built to handle.
insights.quote: Modern AI agents increasingly rely on search infrastructure to execute complex, neuro-symbolic reasoning workflows. These workflows often compile into deeply nested, non-monotonic Boolean queries over text fields.
insights.locator: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal abstract

themes.theme: Theoretical limits of existing query evaluation strategies

insights.claim: Stateful iterator (Document-at-a-Time) query evaluation is structurally bounded by NC^1 formula evaluation and suffers a worst-case O(2^|Q|) exponential blowup in query complexity when unrolling re-convergent logic, meaning it can become computationally intractable on complex nested Boolean queries.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Systems using the common Document-at-a-Time evaluation model will hit exponential slowdowns on the kind of nested Boolean queries AI agents now generate, a latent performance cliff for production search systems.
insights.quote: Stateful iterator models (Document-at-a-Time) are structurally bounded by NC^1 formula evaluation, suffering a worst-case O(2^|Q|) exponential blowup in query complexity when unrolling re-convergent logic.
insights.locator: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal abstract

insights.claim: Recursive materialization (Term-at-a-Time) query evaluation incurs an Omega(|U|) space complexity penalty, the 'Universal Scan', when evaluating logical negation over the full document universe, imposing a costly alternative failure mode to the exponential blowup of Document-at-a-Time evaluation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The other dominant query-evaluation paradigm trades exponential time for linear-in-corpus-size space cost on negation, so at web/enterprise scale it becomes memory-prohibitive; neither standard approach scales to complex negated Boolean logic.
insights.quote: recursive materialization models (Term-at-a-Time) incur an Ω(|U|) space complexity penalty (the Universal Scan) when evaluating logical negation over the document universe
insights.locator: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal abstract

insights.claim: The paper formally proves that evaluating a retrieval language of Boolean queries expressed as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) is strictly P-Complete, establishing a hard theoretical ceiling on how efficiently such queries can be evaluated over an inverted index.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A P-Completeness proof tells engineers there is no algorithmic shortcut (no better-than-polynomial or highly parallelizable solution) for this class of query, so effort should go into practical constant-factor and heuristic optimizations rather than searching for an asymptotically faster general algorithm.
insights.quote: We formalize a retrieval language (L_R) based on Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and prove that its evaluation problem is strictly P-Complete.
insights.locator: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal abstract

themes.theme: ComputePN: a practical algorithm within the theoretical bound

insights.claim: ComputePN, a deterministic, sparsity-aware evaluation algorithm, decouples logical negation from universe-scale materialization via a Positive-Negative dual representation and uses native DAG memoization to strictly bound evaluation time to O(|Q| · |U_active|), avoiding both the exponential blowup of Document-at-a-Time and the universal-scan penalty of Term-at-a-Time evaluation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: ComputePN offers a concrete, implementable evaluation strategy that sidesteps both known failure modes, giving search-infrastructure teams a practical algorithm to adopt for handling complex agent-generated Boolean queries without hitting exponential time or full-corpus space costs.
insights.quote: ComputePN strictly bounds evaluation time to O(|Q| · |U_active|)
insights.locator: The P-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal abstract
